{{Quote|If they're down here, sir, we'll find them.|[[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]]|<ref name="SWE1" />}}
'''OOM command battle droids''' were any [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droids]] used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] for the purposes of transmitting orders from the [[Central Control Computer/Legends|Central Control Computer]] to squads of infantry or [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|security battle droids]]. Until the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the commanders were the only OOM units to possess intelligence and independence apart from the Central Control Computer. A notable command battle droid was [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]], who commanded the droid forces in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:OOMCommandBattleDroid-HeroesOnBothSides.png|thumb|left|200px|Some OOM commanders were equipped with backpacks and had additional yellow markings on their arms.]]
The [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM]] [[Commander/Legends|command]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] were constructed by [[Baktoid Combat Automata/Legends|Baktoid Combat Automata]]<ref name="Databank" /> and had a set of [[Color/Legends|black]] sensors along with tan plating. The [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were 1.91 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height. Yellow markings on their torsos and heads marked their status as command battle droids.<ref name="Databank" /> 

They contained programming which allowed them to adapt to circumstances, which sometimes malfunctioned.<ref name="CCGTPL">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=Battle Droid Officer}}</ref> They received long-distance signals allowing them to be far from base with their squads, and reported directly to the [[Central Control Computer/Legends|Central Control Computer]].<ref name="VisGuide">''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> If a command droid lost contact with a CCC, it would remain active for three minutes, upon which time it would enter standby mode for a further ten minutes, after which it shut down completely.<ref name="Naboo">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Expandsect}}
The OOM command battle droids were deployed as part of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], OOM commanders, along with organic [[Officer/Legends|officers]], took charge of regular [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|infantry]] droids.<ref name="VisGuide" /> OOM command battle droids were in charge of the droids sent to hunt [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]].<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] reported directly to [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]. After the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] was [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|destroyed]], all the droid units on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] shut down.<ref name="SWE1" />

[[File:Maridun_OOM_macrobinoculars.png|thumb|right|200px|An OOM commander on [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]] using [[Macrobinoculars/Legends|macrobinoculars]].]]
Trade Federation OOM command droids joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]].<ref name="SWE2" /> Battle droid officers led company-level formations<ref name="EGW" /> and were assigned as [[Captain/Legends|captains]] of Separatist [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Certain battle droids were granted additional programming and assigned as officers.<ref name="Ambush">{{TCW|Ambush}}</ref> Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|demise]] of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]], all units of the Separatist Droid Army were deactivated,<ref name="SWE3">{{Film|III}}</ref> barring those used by [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]].<ref name="EGW" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:OOMCommandBattleDroid-CargoOfDoom.png|thumb|left|200px|An OOM Commander active during the Clone Wars, showcasing the additional yellow coloring applied on some units' arm joints.]]
Battle droid commanders first appeared in the 1999 film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] and its tie-ins, one example being Command Officer OOM-9. These specialist models were first identified as belonging to an "OOM Series" in the 2002 Revised Edition of the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Arms">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref>

Prior to the release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], it was claimed that the command droids' intelligence and independence were traits they shared with the security battle droids,<ref name="Star Wars: Invasion of Theed Adventure Game">[[Star Wars: Invasion of Theed Adventure Game|''Star Wars: Invasion of Theed'' Adventure Game]]</ref><ref name="Naboo" /> both possessing low-grade electronic brains that differentiated them from pilot and infantry droids.<ref name="Naboo" /> Other sources state that all battle droid types had structurally identical control signal receivers and simple processors, each pre-programmed with specialized subroutines to increase efficiency for their specific job function.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>
